match_id: ARTETA: “WE ARE ONE GAME AWAY FROM WINNING THE PREMIER LEAGUE!”  Arsenal_Burnley_2026-05-18_X2j2aswl-sE
team: ARTETA: “WE ARE ONE GAME AWAY FROM WINNING THE PREMIER LEAGUE!”  Arsenal
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Hi, everyone. Raise your hand if you have a  question, come to you. Let’s go, Sam. Sky first.  
The game you expected? I knew it was going to be  tough. I think in the first half we played some of  
the best football that we have played this season.  We were very unfortunate not to score two or  
three goals, and then there was the story of the  season as well. If we cannot do that, make sure  
that we are extremely efficient defending certain  moments, not giving anything away to the opponent  
and winning the three points. You said it is the  story of the season. You have not conceded from  
open play since the Man City game. Has something  happened, or how do you explain that there has  
been some shift? Well, I think the desire every  single player shows in their defensive duties,  
their behaviours, the way they work for each  other is phenomenal. It is a lot of work put  
in by all the coaches as well, and we all know  the importance of that and how many results and  
wins we have because of that mechanism. It was  a great team performance, a collective effort,  
but obviously Kai has settled the deal first.  All of the season, it has been such a difficult  
season. Yeah, I think we forget the amount  of players that we have missed for long,  
long periods this season, that they are  exceptional. But that is the merit, I think,  
of this team, that regardless of that,  look where we are. We are one game away  
from winning the Premier League with everything  that we have been through, and that shows how  
strong the mindset and the team is. Was that  one of the reasons you started him tonight?  
I had a feeling that he had to start, and in the  way that they set up, I think he could be really  
difficult to handle, and he showed that. Sorry,  Mikel, it was another night where you had to,  
or I felt like people had to, suffer through the  win. Are you primed for a similar one on Sunday,  
or can you even think like that? I don’t know.  I thought that the amount of hair that I have  
is never going to go away, but I think this job is  going to test it to the limit. Just so close now.  
How do you keep everybody calm and focused with  such a big part of it? We have done what is in our  
hands. Since the Man City game away, we said it is  five games and it was at hand. We have done four,  
there is one to go, unless something beautiful  happens tomorrow night. Congratulations.  
Obviously, you were asked a lot last week about  whether you would watch the game, and you said we  
have got to focus on Burnley. Burnley is done,  so are you going to watch the game tomorrow,  
and how will you go through that experience? I  don’t know how long I am going to watch it. I will  
be there in front of the TV, but I don’t know how  much I am going to be able to watch it. I think  
that is a reality. Just on Kai, would you concede  he was maybe lucky to still be on the pitch after  
that foul? Well, I certainly got worried when  they were checking it. When I looked at the bench,  
they said that it wasn’t, but I haven’t had a look  at the action. Following on from that question  
about the games tomorrow, will you watch it,  rewatch it with the players at all? No, I haven’t  
planned to do that. I am planning to watch it with  my family, and again, I don’t know for how long.  
At the end, when you did that speech on the pitch  and you looked around, obviously it was very  
loud and it took you a while to get your words out  because of the noise, what was going through your  
head as you looked around? That it is incredible  to witness what we have created in this stadium.  
Obviously, I have memories from the past and the  comparison is unbelievable to watch. I am so proud  
of that. Today they have created something so  special outside the stadium and in the stadium,  
and now we have set the standards that, as  I said, we are all responsible to maintain,  
because we can provide that. We know the outcome.  How different was that from last season when you  
did your end-of-season speech? The themes compared  from then to now? Well, at that point I think we  
knew that we were going to finish second and we  didn’t have another final to play. So, yeah, what  
I said to them: see you at Selhurst Park and then  City and Budapest. So another two to play. Mikel,  
when we heard from Heck before you went to West  Ham, he was confessing he was basically at West  
Ham for 24 hours. The biggest ever hope of Andoni  and all the players and all the people that are  
supporters of Bournemouth. I think we are all  over, because we know that means if tomorrow they  
get a result for us. I don’t think it is needed.  I mean, what he has done in that football club,  
the transformation and what they are playing for,  I don’t think they need anything else. When you  
look at how Burnley played today, the spirit  that they showed, how difficult they made it,  
so imagine tomorrow. Strong reports are that  Pep Guardiola will leave Man City after this  
season. Now it looks very close, tied up.  Does that change the dynamic this week,  
and what do you feel about maybe him leaving?  No, I cannot comment on that. I think  
the day that he makes the decision to stay or  leave, then we can comment, I think. Thank you.
title: ARTETA: “WE ARE ONE GAME AWAY FROM WINNING THE PREMIER LEAGUE!”  Arsenal 1-0 Burnley
